summary: Rosemary Radford Ruether was a religious studies scholar who studied at Claremont School of Theology (~1960–1965). She held a post at Howard University from circa 1965 to 1975.

Rosina Pastore is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She earned an MA from the University of Naples "L'Orientale", studied at Visva-Bharati, and completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne under Maya Burger and Stefania Cavaliere, later working at Ghent University.

Ross Arthur Leslie Moore was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He was educated at Dulwich College and Peterhouse, Cambridge (~1880–1883), where he later served as Lecturer in Marathi from 1921 to 1927.

Ross Bolleter is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Western Australia and trained under David Tunley, John Tarrant, and Robert Baker Aitken. From circa 1988 to 2023, he served as a Zen teacher with the Zen Group of Western Australia.

Rotem Geva is a historian and Indologist. She earned an MA at The New School (2005–2007) and a PhD at Princeton University (2007–2014), and served as Department Chair at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 2016.

Roy Rappaport was a religious studies and anthropology scholar who completed his doctorate at Columbia University (~1959–1966). He served as Chair of the Department of Anthropology at the University of Michigan (~1965–1997) and was president of the American Anthropological Association.

Roy Tzohar works in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Tel Aviv University and earning his PhD at Columbia University under Gary A. Tubb, he held posts at Columbia, the Max Planck Institute, the Free University of Berlin, and Tel Aviv University.

Roy W. Perrett is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Canterbury and the University of Otago. He held positions at Massey University (~1988–2004), the University of Melbourne (~2004–2007), and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~2008–2011).

Royal W. Weiler was an Indologist and linguist who completed his BA and PhD under W. Norman Brown at the University of Pennsylvania. He taught at Columbia University (~1958–1963) and was Assistant Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (~1963–1978).

Royall Tyler is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies. Educated at Harvard and Columbia under Donald Keene, he held teaching posts at Wisconsin-Madison, Ohio State, and the University of Oslo, headed the Japan Centre at Australian National University, and visited Harvard.
Royce Wiles is an Indologist who earned his PhD from the Australian National University by 2000, where his affiliation was attested between 1997 and 2000.

Rozaliya Osipovna Shor was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Vsevolod Miller. She held research posts at RANION, the State Academy of Artistic Sciences, and the Institute of Oriental Studies, and professorships at Baku, Moscow, and Leningrad institutes.

Ruben L. F. Habito is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies educated at Ateneo de Manila, Sophia University, and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Sophia University and Ryukoku University, founded Maria Kannon Zen Center, and became Professor at SMU.
Rudi Paret was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tübingen (~1920–1924). He held posts at the University of Bonn (~1940–1951) and the University of Tübingen (~1951–1968).

Rudolf Carnap was a philosopher who studied at Jena, Freiburg, Berlin, and Vienna. He held academic posts at the University of Vienna (1926), Charles University (1931), the University of Chicago (1936–1952), and the University of California, Los Angeles (1954).

Rudolf Ernst Wilhelm Meyer was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Heidelberg University and completed his PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1873–1877) under Albrecht Weber and Johannes Schmidt.

Rudolf Fuchs was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the Humboldt University of Berlin by 1908 under the supervision of Richard Pischel, studying with scholars such as Albrecht Weber and Heinrich Zimmer.
Rudolf Geiger studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from circa 1913 to 1917 and held an academic post at the University of Munich from circa 1937 to 1958.

Rudolf Haym was a scholar of philosophy and history who attended Cöllnisches Gymnasium, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, and Frederick William University Berlin. He held an academic post at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1868.

Rudolf Kaschewsky was a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cologne and Bonn, taught Tibetan at Goethe University Frankfurt, and served as an academic official at the University of Bonn (1974–2004).
